next_event.source: No Investor Day or new three-year objectives date found in Baba corpus (lexical 'Investor Day' FY2026 search, doc 117964 Q4 FY2026 call); last Investor Day was 2023 (doc 96058, doc 69634) and the FY2023-FY2026 three-year cycle ended 2026-06-30, so a new cycle is due but unscheduled.

margin_framing.metric_basis_note: Management guides adjusted operating income (AOI) margin, not EBITDA; the gap test compares the AOI guide with VA consensus 'Operating margin' (FY2026 consensus actual 20.52% matches the reported 20.5% AOI margin).

statements.speaker: Ash Ghei
statements.doc_title: Broadridge Financial Solutions Inc Q4 2026 Earnings Call

statements.quote: In the past, we have always talked about a 50 basis point sort of average increase in margins per year. [...] We have been talking about over time, we still continue to expect 50 basis points.
statements.speaker: Tim Gokey
statements.doc_title: 53rd Annual JPMorgan Global Technology, Media and Communications Conference

statements.quote: we communicated, reaffirmed our guidance for our 2023 to 2026 views, which calls for 5%-8% recurring revenue growth, 1%-2 percentage points from M&A, 8%-12% earnings growth, and 50 basis points plus of margin expansion.
statements.speaker: Ashima Ghei

street.gap_assumption: Fiscal year ends June; Baba FY-2027 = company fiscal 2027 (July 2026 to June 2027). Compares the ~21% FY2027 AOI margin guide with VA consensus FY-2027 operating margin 20.844%; FY2026 EBITDA margin is reported actual.
street.source: Baba data_financials consensus (summary and fundamentals, Visible Alpha)

evidence_of_progress.note: Order is [Q3 FY2026, Q4 FY2026]. Q3 FY2026 AOI margin 21.5%, down 90 bps YoY, 80 bps from distribution pass-through and lower rates (Ghei, doc 197508, 2026-04-30). Q4 FY2026 AOI margin 26.9%, down 10 bps YoY (Ghei, doc 117964, 2026-08-04). Full-year FY2026 AOI margin 20.5%, 'rose slightly'.

disqualifier_reason: Margin target already reflected in consensus: the FY2027 ~21% AOI margin guide sits only 16 bps above VA consensus operating margin of 20.84%. No CEO or CFO change in the 18-month window (CFO Ghei appointed 2024-12-16; CEO Gokey since 2019-01-02); only board refresh and tuck-in M&A.
verdict: Not a GXO setup: cheap and de-rated, but a high-margin, long-tenured management team guiding a one-year 50 bps step the street already models, with no leadership catalyst.
open_questions: When and where will Broadridge publish its next three-year objectives now that the FY2023 to FY2026 cycle has closed, and will the 50 bps a year core margin rate be restated with a horizon?
Does adding President Christopher Perry to the board in February 2026 signal a CEO succession plan for Gokey (93 months in seat)?
How much reported margin uplift would the SEC eDelivery rule deliver after fiscal 2027 from lower pass-through distribution revenue?
